title: Baidyanath — Risk & Reputation Research
content:
According to reviews on PissedConsumer and Trustpilot, Baidyanath customers frequently complain about order delays, missing deliveries, and unresponsive customer service. Specific complaints include wrong or short quantities received, damaged or defective items, and allegations of fake products. Some customers report slow or non-processed refunds and exchanges. Negative reviews also mention prepaid orders not delivered and refunds withheld. Conversely, some users call Baidyanath a good ayurveda brand and describe staff as helpful in limited cases. Trustpilot reviews highlight issues like receiving products filled with dead bugs and non-receipt of medicines despite payment.

- Expect order delays and missing deliveries; many customer complaints focus on delivery of goods.
- Customer service often unresponsive; phone and email contacts may not connect.
- Refunds and exchanges reported as slow or not processed.
- Several reviewers advise buying from Flipkart or Amazon instead.

According to customer reviews on PissedConsumer, Baidyanath is often criticized for order delays, missing deliveries, unresponsive customer service, and slow or non-existent refunds and exchanges. The company's terms and conditions state that they will not compensate for delays and are not responsible for any delivery issues due to unforeseen circumstances. The shipping policy mentions that if a non-delivery occurs due to user error, extra costs for re-delivery will be claimed from the user. Additionally, Baidyanath reserves the right to cancel orders for incorrect pricing or other reasons. Some users recommend buying from Flipkart or Amazon instead.

The sources mention two legal disputes involving Baidyanath. One is a products liability case in New York where a default judgment was awarded against Baidyanath after the manufacturer failed to respond to the consumer's efforts to contact them. The other is a trademark infringement case in India where Dabur India Limited sought an injunction against Baidyanath for broadcasting certain advertisements. The sources do not provide a definitive answer regarding the outcome of the trademark case.
